title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 202
paragraphs: These were the Greeks who awaited the Persian attack in this place: of the Spartans, three hundred hoplites; of the men of Tegea and Mantineia, a thousand, half from each; from Orchomenos in Arcadia, one hundred and twenty; and from the rest of Arcadia, a thousand — so many Arcadians in all. From Corinth, four hundred; from Phlius, two hundred; and from Mykene, eighty: these were the contingents from the Peloponnese. From the Boeotians came seven hundred of the Thespians and four hundred of the Thebans.
